Ore Factory Squad is one of those games that I started playing thinking, "I'll just play for a little while," and then somehow realized I'd been playing for hours.

The core gameplay loop is incredibly satisfying. You start with very little, begin digging for resources, process what you find, sell it, reinvest the money, upgrade your equipment, and slowly turn a small mining operation into a proper industrial factory.

And honestly, that progression is probably my favorite part of the game.

At the beginning, you're doing almost everything yourself. You're mining, collecting resources, moving things around, figuring out the systems, and trying to make enough money to improve your operation. But as you progress, you unlock better equipment, machines, automation, transportation, production options, and other upgrades.

Eventually, you go from basically being a person with a shovel to running an entire mining and manufacturing operation.

The mining is also a lot of fun.

The underground terrain being diggable and procedurally generated makes exploring for resources much more interesting than simply walking between predetermined resource nodes. You actually get to decide where you dig and how you approach the underground.

Starting with basic tools and eventually working toward more powerful equipment gives the mining a really nice sense of progression. You can genuinely feel your operation becoming more capable as you upgrade.

Then you have the factory side of the game, which is where things can get dangerously addictive for anyone who enjoys automation games.

You start thinking:

"Okay, I can make this."

Then:

"How can I make this faster?"

Then:

"Why am I manually doing this when I could automate it?"

And suddenly you're rearranging machines, conveyors, storage, and production lines because you absolutely NEED to make everything more efficient.

That progression from manual work to automation is incredibly satisfying.

The combination of mining and factory management is what makes Ore Factory Squad stand out to me.

You get the relaxing side of digging and gathering resources, combined with the more strategic side of production, logistics, contracts, upgrades, and expansion.

If you get tired of one side of the game, there's usually something else to work on.

Want to mine? Go dig.

Want to improve the factory? Start building.

Want to make more money? Improve your production.

Want to optimize everything? Congratulations, you're now staring at conveyor belts for the next hour.

The progression is especially satisfying.

There's always another upgrade or improvement to work toward. You're constantly making the operation more efficient, and your upgrades actually feel meaningful.

You're not just making money because there's a number going up. You're making money so you can buy better equipment, which lets you mine more efficiently, which lets you produce more, which lets you fulfill better contracts, which lets you expand even further.

It's a very satisfying gameplay loop.

I also really like the economy and production systems. You aren't necessarily just mining something and immediately selling it. You can process resources, create more valuable products, fulfill contracts, manage deliveries, and decide how you want to grow your operation.

That gives you actual decisions to make and keeps the game from feeling like you're repeating exactly the same task forever.

The logistics side is surprisingly fun too.

Forklifts, trucks, storage, transportation, warehouses, and production lines might not sound exciting on paper, but once you have a factory running, you start caring about every little part of the process.

You start noticing bottlenecks.

You wonder why something isn't moving.

You realize one machine isn't producing fast enough.

You move something slightly.

Suddenly everything works.

And somehow that feels like a major accomplishment.

That's the kind of game Ore Factory Squad is: it makes you feel proud about solving problems that you probably wouldn't care about in any other game.

The co-op is another huge plus.

Playing with friends makes the whole operation feel like an actual team effort. One person can focus on mining, someone else can work on the factory, another person can handle transportation or logistics, and everyone contributes toward expanding the business.

Of course, there will also be the inevitable moment when someone completely ignores the carefully planned production system and starts doing something ridiculous.

That's part of the fun.

The ability to play with up to four people makes this a great game for a small group of friends, especially if everyone enjoys management, automation, or simulation games.

At the same time, I appreciate that it can also be played solo. If you're the kind of player who likes taking your time, organizing everything exactly how you want it, and building an efficient operation without anyone messing up your plans, there's plenty here to enjoy on your own.

Another thing I really enjoy is seeing the factory physically grow.

You start with a small setup and gradually turn it into something much larger. Your factory becomes something that feels like it belongs to you because you've built and organized it yourself.

Being able to look around after several hours and think, "I built all of this," is one of the best feelings these types of games can provide.

The game also has a surprisingly relaxing atmosphere. There are plenty of moments where you're just mining, organizing resources, watching machines run, or improving your setup, and it's incredibly easy to get into that "just one more thing" mindset.

You finish one task.

Then another.

Then you decide to upgrade something.

Then you need more resources for the upgrade.

So you go mining.

Then you come back and process everything.

Then you notice your production line could be more efficient.

And suddenly several hours have disappeared.

That is usually a very good sign for a simulation game.

There are definitely things I'd still like to see improved or expanded over time. Like most games in this genre, there are systems that could be smoother or more intuitive, and I'd love to see even more machines, resources, production chains, customization options, locations, and reasons to keep expanding an established factory.

But honestly, those are the kinds of complaints I don't mind having.

I'd much rather finish a game session thinking "I want MORE of this" than wondering why I was playing in the first place.

At the end of the day, Ore Factory Squad works because the basic gameplay loop is just really satisfying:

Mine.
Process.
Build.
Automate.
Sell.
Upgrade.
Expand.
Repeat.

It sounds simple when you put it that way, but once all of those systems start interacting with each other, it's incredibly easy to lose yourself in the game.

If you enjoy mining, factory building, automation, logistics, resource gathering, management, simulation, or progression, I think Ore Factory Squad is absolutely worth checking out.

And if you have a few friends who enjoy those kinds of games, even better.

There is something genuinely fun about starting with practically nothing and gradually turning your little operation into a huge production system together.

Ore Factory Squad isn't trying to reinvent every genre it touches, but it doesn't need to. It takes a bunch of mechanics that are already fun individually and combines them into a gameplay loop that works really well.

The mining is satisfying.
The factory building is addictive.
The automation is fun.
The progression feels rewarding.
The contracts give you goals.
The logistics give you plenty to manage.
And the co-op gives you the opportunity to either build an incredibly efficient operation or completely destroy it with your friends.

That's a win in my book.

Now excuse me while I go "fix one tiny thing" in my factory for the next four hours.

Wir haben Ore Factory Squad komplett im Koop durchgespielt und nach ca. 34 Stunden alle Errungenschaften erreicht.

Grundsätzlich ist das Spiel nicht schlecht. Bei uns lief es nahezu bugfrei, und gerade im Koop hatten wir definitiv unseren Spaß. Der Reiz, die eigene Produktion weiter auszubauen, Mitarbeiter einzustellen und Stück für Stück voranzukommen, funktioniert gut. Es gibt definitiv einen gewissen Suchtfaktor.

Allerdings hat das Spiel aus unserer Sicht ein großes Problem: Man ist einfach viel zu schnell am Ende.

Gerade das Abbauen ist am Anfang extrem mühsam. Wir haben teilweise stundenlang nur damit verbracht, Material abzubauen, und irgendwann hat es sich eher wie Arbeit als wie ein Spiel angefühlt. Gleichzeitig erreicht man Level 10 ziemlich schnell. Sobald das geschafft ist, fehlt leider ein großer Teil der Motivation weiterzumachen, weil es nichts mehr Neues zu entdecken oder freizuschalten gibt.

Hier hätten wir uns deutlich mehr gewünscht:

-mehr Level
-mehr Maschinen
-weitere Lizenzen und Produktionsmöglichkeiten
-neue Erze und Ressourcen
-zusätzliche Maps zum Freischalten

Auch einige vorhandene Elemente fühlen sich leider etwas ungenutzt an. Zum Beispiel gibt es eine Tankstelle, mit der man aktuell nicht wirklich etwas anfangen kann. Hier hätte man den Kauf von Benzin für Fahrzeuge oder Maschinen integrieren können.

Auf der höchsten Ausbaustufe hätten wir uns außerdem von Dynamit, Hacke, Schaufel und Presslufthammer deutlich mehr "Wumms" gewünscht. Wenn man schon die besten Werkzeuge besitzt, sollte sich das auch entsprechend bemerkbar machen. Ein größerer Abbaubereich und deutlich mehr Schaden wären hier schön gewesen. Wirklich viel Unterschied gabs nicht. 

Die Maps sind grundsätzlich nicht schlecht gestaltet und ein paar kleine Dinge sorgten trotzdem immer wieder für Lacher – beispielsweise das permanente Hupen, Autos umfahren oder das Herumtorkeln nach einem Besuch in der Bar. Solche Kleinigkeiten lockern das Spiel angenehm auf.

Fazit:

Der Suchtfaktor ist definitiv vorhanden, und gerade im Koop macht Ore Factory Squad Spaß. Für uns war nach rund 34 Stunden inklusive aller Errungenschaften allerdings einfach die Luft raus.

Das Spiel hat eine gute Grundlage und wir hatten durchaus eine schöne Zeit damit. Mit mehr Leveln, Maschinen, Lizenzen, Maps, Erzen und einem umfangreicheren Endgame hätte daraus aber deutlich mehr werden können.

Deshalb 7/10 Punkten bzw. „Ausgeglichen“.

Einen Daumen runter verdient das Spiel definitiv nicht – dafür hatten wir zu viel Spaß damit. Aber für einen Daumen hoch fehlt uns momentan einfach Content und Langzeitmotivation.

I enjoy the core loop of the game. Go to your land, start digging, take your goods home, process them in your factory, then use your materials and processed goods to complete orders. 

The digging is as fun as you'd expect (so if you don't think digging for ore is fun, you won't like it) with nice little upgrades as you progress to make things a bit easier. Digging is the core of the game and I think they are doing well trying to stick with that. There are workers you can send out to sites to basically gather materials without having to do it yourself. I imagine as you grow, you'll probably end up getting most of your materials that way as well. 

The factory portion is probably what I'd say elevates this simulator beyond just a digging sim. If you enjoy factory automation, this does it pretty well. I'm not huge into automation games like Factorio so I can't speak for how well its systems are, but it having drawn me in as much as it did speaks for something at the very least. 

Overall, this is a fun game. Definitely still feels early access and there are a lot of improvements to be made, but what's there is still a lot of fun. I've only stopped playing it because I want to wait for more updates to come out, otherwise I'd likely just end up burning myself out on playing it. It's addicting and fun, and I'm sure if you played it with friends it'd be a good time. Definitely a podcast and chill game. And for ~$10? Easy purchase if you think this might be your thing.

[h1]Унылый симулятор рутины: красиво в трейлере, невыносимо скучно в игре![/h1]

Не видитесь на положительные отзывы и красивые ролики. Если вы играли хотя бы в одну нормальную игру про автоматизацию (Factorio или Satisfactory), здесь вы просто умрете от тоски. Игра безумно скучная, пустая и приедается практически мгновенно. 

Весь игровой процесс — это примитивный цикл: поковырял землю киркой, закинул руду в плавильню, проложил одну прямую конвейерную ленту. Всё. Здесь нет сложных логических цепочек, нет вызова для ума, нет никакого менеджмента. Механики плоские, как картон.

Мертвый мир. Вокруг вас — абсолютно пустая, безжизненная коробка. Никакого исследования, никаких скрытых секретов, никакого интерактива. Ощущение, что ты просто выполняешь механическую работу на конвейере в пустом ангаре.

Кооператив игру не спасает. Рассказы про «веселый хаос вчетвером» — обычный миф. Если игра скучная в соло, то вчетвером вы просто будете страдать от скуки коллективно, быстрее выедая тот мизерный объем контента, который здесь есть.

**Recommended 👍**

Ore Factory Squad is a really fun game and, especially when playing with friends, it can easily give you several hours of entertainment. The idea of starting with almost nothing, mining resources, expanding your factory, and eventually automating a large part of the production works really well.

It’s important to keep in mind that the game is still in **Early Access**, so there’s obviously a lot more to come. I’m personally looking forward to the updates promised in the roadmap because the foundation is solid and the game has a lot of potential.

That said, not everything is perfect. After a while, the game becomes quite **repetitive**, and once you have almost everything unlocked, there isn’t enough content or enough new goals to keep you playing.

There are also several things that could be improved:

* **The robots need a lot of work.** They can’t properly move underneath some conveyor belts, constantly get stuck, and you have to use the unstuck option. Even after doing that, sometimes they still refuse to work properly. I have every robot upgrade and every achievement in the game, so I’ve spent enough time with this system to know how frustrating it can be.

* **Factory automation is too limited.** The concept is great, but the available space and, especially, the number and placement of material input points prevent you from building a factory as automated as you would like.

* **Contracts should be much better integrated with automation.** If I accept a contract and already have the required materials in storage or available in the material feeders, it would be great if the factory could automatically start producing what is needed.

* Taking that idea further, **robots should be able to automatically accept contracts, complete them, and deliver them** once production is finished. That would allow you to eventually build a truly autonomous factory, which I think should be one of the main endgame goals.

* The **stock system** should count not only what is sitting in storage, but also the materials currently inside machines and material feeders. Once your factory becomes large, this would make managing everything much easier.

* It would also be great if the **workers you hire were physically present with you in the mine**, actually working and moving around. Right now, the game lacks that feeling of running a mining operation that gradually becomes bigger, busier, and more alive.

* And then there’s the **excavator...** It definitely needs another look. The idea of operating heavy machinery is great, but the controls and overall handling leave a lot to be desired and can make it more frustrating than useful.

The endgame could also use more options: larger factories, more machinery, new automation systems, special contracts, or simply more reasons to keep optimizing your production once you have unlocked all the upgrades.

Despite all of this, **I recommend Ore Factory Squad**. I’ve had a lot of fun with it and I think it has a very solid foundation. The main problem right now is that eventually you reach a point where you’ve basically seen everything the game has to offer.

If the developers deliver on the roadmap, improve automation, fix the robot issues, and add more late-game content, this could become a really great mining and factory automation game.

**For now: recommended, especially with friends, but there is still plenty of room for improvement.**

This game looks like much of what I enjoy in a game - logistics, exploration, tech trees... And yes, it technically is, but everything falls short of other executions.

Because the cycle is always "make material, sell or upgrade material to sell" the progression is shallower than most games where your tiers of products have to keep building. You only ever need money to buy machines and upgrades, so you can simply pick contracts that match what you're producing instead of having to balance all possible production. It has echoes of games like Factorio, Satisfactory, Foundry, or Dyson Sphere Project but never feels like it grows out of the first two tiers of tech.

Similarly, the exploration quickly becomes tedious. It's fun to dig for ore for a while. Then you realize it's the exact same thing in a different location, which you can't even see because you're underground. Sure, you'll occasionally find caves, but that's basically like digging up a treasure chest in the wall. You have to avoid hazards, but that just means digging carefully in one place.

I wanted to like it. Maybe they'll incorporate reasons to build specific resources beyond contracts in the future. I'll check it out after a couple upgrades, but for now it's uninstalled.

Great co-op game with a lot of potential

My friends and I really enjoyed playing Ore Factory Squad in co-op. Building and optimizing the factory together works really well, and there was always something fun to do.

However, we felt that you can progress through the game relatively quickly. I would love to see more content in the future, especially more advanced automation mechanics.

For example, it would be really cool to have robots that could automatically deliver the correct materials to specific machines. I would also love to see more advanced conveyor belt systems. At the moment, a conveyor belt continuously delivers one type of material as long as that material is available at the output. It would be much more interesting if machines could request specific materials and the conveyor system would then deliver exactly what is needed.

Right now, we usually just throw most of our resources into the material output. This basically gives us an unlimited storage system and makes the whole idea of properly organizing and managing a pallet warehouse somewhat pointless.

Overall, though, this is a really enjoyable co-op game that we had a lot of fun with. With more content and deeper automation mechanics, I think Ore Factory Squad could reach its full potential and become an even better game!

Mir und meinen Freunden hat Ore Factory Squad im Koop wirklich sehr viel Spaß gemacht. Besonders das gemeinsame Aufbauen und Optimieren der Fabrik funktioniert richtig gut, und der Spielspaß bleibt eigentlich durchgehend erhalten.

Allerdings kommt man meiner Meinung nach relativ schnell durch das Spiel. Ich würde mir deshalb in Zukunft noch mehr Inhalte und vor allem komplexere Automatisierungsmöglichkeiten wünschen.

Besonders cool wären zum Beispiel Roboter, die selbstständig die passenden Materialien zu den jeweiligen Maschinen bringen. Auch bei den Förderbändern würde ich mir mehr Möglichkeiten wünschen: Aktuell liefern sie ein Material dauerhaft, solange sich dieses am Materialausgang befindet. Interessanter wäre ein System, bei dem Maschinen gezielt ein bestimmtes Material anfordern können und das Förderband daraufhin genau dieses Material liefert.

Momentan werfen wir deshalb einen Großteil der Ressourcen einfach in den Materialausgang. Dadurch hat man praktisch ein unendlich großes Lager, wodurch der eigentliche Sinn eines gut organisierten Palettenlagers etwas verloren geht.

Insgesamt aber ein wirklich gelungenes Koop-Spiel, das uns viel Spaß gemacht hat. Mit mehr Content und tiefergehender Automatisierung könnte Ore Factory Squad noch deutlich mehr aus seinem Potenzial herausholen!

[h2]圧倒的「チル」なプレイスタイルが魅力[/h2]
本作の基本は「鉱物を掘る → 加工する → 出荷してお金を稼ぐ → 設備をアップグレードする」という非常にシンプルなループです。「親の莫大な借金を返済する」ような重いノルマや最終目標はなく、ひたすら自分のペースで工場を拡張していけます。

[h2]ペナルティのゆるい「徹夜」システム[/h2]
ソロプレイには時間経過と疲労の概念があります。夜になるとシステムから就寝を促されますが、実は[b]好きなだけ作業を続行可能[/b]です。
徹夜のペナルティは「眠気で照準が時々ぶれる」「ツールの使用速度が少し落ちる」程度。工場内での作業に至っては実質ペナルティなしで、好きなだけ”残業”できます。

[h2]ちょっとした攻略情報：崩落システムの活用[/h2]
実は、採掘時に「地面に設置している面がない状態（支えがない状態）」になると、上のブロックが自動で崩れます。これを活用して足元をうまく掘り進めると、[b]広範囲の土砂を一気にきれいに除去できて非常に爽快[/b]です。手作業のちょっとした時短テクニックとして役立ちます。

要するにこのゲームは、Factorioに代表される「工場自動化系ゲーム」ではないということだ。
ゲームは「採掘」と「生産」の2つに分かれるが、どちらも自動化はできない。

採掘パートは完全に手動。レーダーを使って(使わなくてもいいが)黙々と掘り進める。ディグダグもしくはミスタードリラーな気分。ちなみに後半の土地では爆弾が掘り出されて即死したりする。

I don't really like the term 'friendslop' because it implies low-effort, probably vibe-coded, multi-player games that are churned out with little care and quickly abandoned.

This game is certainly not that. Whilst I'd argue it's more an early-access game than a full release, what's already there is more than enough to get value for money and there's a lot more to come in the next year and, so far, the developers have made good on their promise for consistent updates.

The basic game has you set up a small mining business. So small, in fact, your first plot of land is someone's back yard. From this you use basic shovels to excavated various minerals to be either sold or taken to your factory and turned into products for other industries.

It's slow going at first. Which is where your friends can help. You and up to three others can make short work of the plot of land and divide duties between mining, logistics, and manufacture.  The entire game is designed around this loop. Dig, carry, manufacture, sell, invest, upgrade. In a relatively short amount of time you can have a fully automated factory of machines and conveyors producing ores, minerals, products and electronics. While robots ferry the pallets from machine to storage and from storage to delivery van. It's all very satisfying. 

I've found that it's fun to play solo, too. Although it's preferred that you play with friends, it's entirely possible, with smart investment and some hard work, to find NPC miners who will excavated land for you while you concentrate on finding and fulfilling contracts. It's not as fast as when you have a group but it's possible to make a good profit and still max out your factory without it feeling like a slog.

There's recently been a free expansion where factory owners can now own an oil refinery but I haven't been able to try it out yet. I'm definitely looking forward to it.

I recommend that players join their discord. The developers are active on there, answering questions, taking feedback, noting and quickly addressing bugs that players report. It's a really nice community there and no question goes ignored.

I absolutely recommend the game. The graphics are pretty decent, it runs well, and the gameplay loop is exactly what you expect from these business sim games. Yet it delivers it at a lower price than many and deserves to be more popular.

Pour un jeu de simulation il est plutôt bien travaillé, assez complet sans nous surcharger d'informations. Nous avons joués à deux mais le multijoueur monte jusqu'à 4, augmentant ainsi le fun et réduisant le temps de jeu necéssaire pour le platine. Il y a quelques bugs (de collision surtout) qui sont assez drôle par moment, heureusement qu'ils ont ajouté un bouton pour se débloquer et débloquer les véhicules. La rejouabilité est ce qu'on demande d'un jeu de simulation à 8€ le début est agréable avec la découverte de nouveau lieu de minage, de nouveaux équipements mais à la longue le jeu devient très répétitif dans les hauts niveaux. L'optimisation et l'automatisation avec les robots est un plus, après que tout soit configuré le jeu est encore plus agréable. 
Pour ce qui est des graphismes le jeu est agréablement épuré mais ce n'est pas non plus une claque visuelle, juste de quoi jouer sans pourrir l'immersion. 

--- AVIS FINAL ---
Je recommande le jeu pour les fans de jeu de simulation sans prise de tête, pour jouer avec des amis le temps de quelques soirées.

Llevo horas metido en Ore Factory Squad y la verdad es que es un título sumamente divertido y adictivo. Aunque he estado jugando en solitario, se nota a leguas que la experiencia con amigos debe ser bestial y multiplicar las risas y la organización.

La jugabilidad cumple a la perfección con lo que buscas en un buen título de gestión y factoría: sales a recolectar materiales en bruto para empezar a procesarlos, pero la verdadera magia empieza cuando desbloqueas la automatización. Con la ayuda de los robots, que se encargan de trasladar los palets de materiales y hasta efectúan las entregas, el flujo de trabajo se vuelve un no parar de satisfacción logística.

Lo que más me ha sorprendido es su rendimiento y estabilidad. Teniendo en cuenta que todavía se encuentra en fase de acceso anticipado, el juego funciona increíblemente bien, sin bugs molestos que arruinen la partida. Si los desarrolladores continúan por este camino y siguen mejorando el proyecto, va a terminar convirtiéndose en una auténtica obra maestra del género.

Lo recomiendo muchísimo si te gusta automatizar  y perder la noción del tiempo. ¡Pruébalo sin dudarlo!
